# Frontier Sector Code — Penal Framework
## Part IX — Penal Code Framework
### Article 48 — Offense Grades
48.1. Offenses are graded from I to V:
- [bold]Grade I — Minor:[/bold] warnings, fines, short detention. - [bold]Grade II — Moderate:[/bold] fines, detention, license suspension. - [bold]Grade III — Serious:[/bold] detention, license revocation, asset seizure. - [bold]Grade IV — Severe:[/bold] long detention, eligibility for permanent confinement, asset forfeiture. - [bold]Grade V — Capital:[/bold] permanent confinement or execution, with Central Command approval.
48.2. The Penal Code shall assign each offense a grade and a sentence range.
### Article 49 — Contraband Tiers
49.1. Contraband is divided into five tiers under Appendix A.
49.2. The Penal Code shall list the specific items in each tier.
### Article 50 — Sentencing Principles
50.1. Sentences are cumulative for separate offenses and separate victims.
50.2. A lesser-included offense may not be stacked on a greater offense for the same act.
50.3. An attempt and a completed offense may not both be charged for the same act and victim.
50.4. Repeat offenders face escalating penalties. The Penal Code may set enhanced ranges for repeated offenses.
50.5. The sentencing authority may reduce a sentence for cooperation, but is not required to do so.
50.6. The Penal Code may set mandatory minimums for Grade IV and Grade V offenses.
### Article 51 — Fines, Restitution, and Forfeiture
51.1. Fines are paid to the Frontier Administration.
51.2. Restitution is paid to victims.
51.3. Instrumentalities and proceeds of crime may be forfeited.
51.4. Fines are scaled to the offender’s ability to pay, but inability to pay does not erase the fine.
51.5. No person may be imprisoned solely for inability to pay a fine. The tribunal may order community service or another lawful alternative.
### Article 52 — Permanent Confinement and Execution
52.1. Permanent confinement is available for Grade IV and Grade V offenses where the Penal Code authorizes it.
52.2. Execution is available only for Grade V offenses: aggravated murder, treason in wartime, or terrorism or mass destruction causing mass casualties.
52.3. Execution requires:
- a tribunal conviction; - an appeal; - approval by Central Command.
52.4. Execution must be humane and may not be made a public spectacle.
52.5. Forced borging is not a lawful punishment. Voluntary borging may be arranged with consent.
52.6. A person who is unable to understand the proceedings may not be executed.
### Article 53 — Criminal Records and Expungement
53.1. Criminal records are public.
53.2. Minor offenses may be expunged after a period set by the Penal Code.
53.3. Sensitive records may be sealed by the Station Representative, Sheriff, or Central Command.
53.4. The NFSD may access sealed records for lawful investigations.
## Appendix A — Contraband Tiers
- [bold]Tier 1 — Minor restricted items:[/bold] non-lethal self-defense weapons, restricted tools, and minor controlled items. Permit required. Low priority without another offense. - [bold]Tier 2 — Moderate restricted items:[/bold] lethal civilian weapons, restricted armor, and controlled pharmaceuticals. Permit required. Investigate if observed. - [bold]Tier 3 — Serious restricted items:[/bold] military-style small arms, explosives, hacking or EMP tools, and hard drugs. Permit required. Investigate and seize. - [bold]Tier 4 — Severe heavy hardware:[/bold] 100–199 damage weapons, heavy weapons, advanced energy weapons, armor-piercing ammunition, and high-grade combat gear. Permit required. Arrestable without a permit. - [bold]Tier 5 — Military and law-enforcement hardware:[/bold] 200+ damage weapons, weapons of mass destruction, chemical or biological weapons, military energy weapons, combat mechs, orbital ordnance, NFSD hardsuits and uniforms, and restricted law-enforcement equipment. TSF military, NFSD, and authorized SolGov officials only. Serious offense.
The Penal Code shall list the specific items in each tier.
## Appendix B — Warrant and Search Procedure
- Warrants are issued by the Station Representative or Sheriff. - If neither is available, the highest-ranking NFSD officer may authorize a warrant with notification to Central Command. - A warrant is required for an extensive or fine-grained search, or for a targeted search of all of a person’s possessions, vessels, and property. - The NFSD may inspect cargo and board and search vessels without a warrant for law-enforcement, customs, or safety purposes. - A search may also proceed without a warrant for consent, immediate danger, destruction of evidence, hot pursuit, customs inspection, safety inspection, or impounded-property inventory. - NFSD should announce their presence unless safety requires otherwise. - Seized property must be receipted. Lawful property is returned when no longer needed. - Unlawfully obtained evidence may be excluded by a tribunal.
## Appendix C — Frontier Tribunal Procedure
- The Frontier Tribunal is composed of citizens of the Sector. (OOC: player-run; uses existing roles.) - The Station Representative, Sheriff, or an agreed citizen presides. - The NFSD, Station Representative, or another SolGov official may prosecute. - The accused may self-represent or choose any available citizen as defense. - Minor offenses may be handled summarily by the NFSD with a warning or fine; the accused may request a tribunal. - Grade III and above require a tribunal hearing. - Grade V requires a tribunal, an appeal, and Central Command approval. - If a tribunal cannot be formed, Central Command reviews the matter. - Proceedings should be prompt and should not unnecessarily disrupt the shift. - Hearings are public unless sensitive information requires sealing.
## OOC Disclaimer
This page is in-character law. It does not replace the server rules. Certain offenses described here may also be violations of the server rules and may result in staff punishment, including bans.
